implementation_notes: Rust's blob is less common because the compiler objects to unused fields and because ownership discourages a god struct, but it appears as one struct holding a client's configuration, a cache, a renderer and a timer, with `impl` blocks added over time. The detection is per-field `rg` counts plus `cargo clippy -- -W dead_code`, and the extraction is one struct per cluster with the owning function receiving only what it needs — which in Rust means the borrow checker will point at exactly the places where the clusters were secretly coupled.
idiom_name: one struct with unrelated fields and many impl blocks' worth of methods
code_sketch:
struct Server {                     // blob
  widgets: HashMap<String, Widget>,   // cluster: render
  buf: Vec<u8>,                       // cluster: protocol
  last: Instant,                      // cluster: timing
}
pitfalls: `#[derive(Default)]` on a large struct makes 'which fields does this function use' invisible without reading the body.
`#[allow(dead_code)]` hides fields that are genuinely part of one cluster but were never wired up.
`pub` fields on a large struct expose the blob's shape to every consumer, so the split cannot be made without a breaking change.
